items.question: Why does DeepWalk’s supervised feature learning objective make it especially strong at node classification on sparse networks?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses a supervised feature learning objective for node classification.
items.correction: DeepWalk is an unsupervised feature learning method that learns vertex representations from random walks, not a supervised classifier.
items.evidence_quote: In this paper we introduce deep learning (unsupervised feature learning) [2] techniques, which have proven successful in natural language processing, into network analysis for the first time.

items.question: How does DeepWalk’s use of content recommendation data help it generalize to missing link prediction tasks?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk is described as using content recommendation data.
items.correction: The passage lists content recommendation as an application area of networks, not as data used by DeepWalk.
items.evidence_quote: Machine learning applications in networks (such as network classification [15, 37], content recommendation [11], anomaly detection [5], and missing link prediction [22]) must be able to deal with this sparsity in order to survive.

items.question: What makes DeepWalk’s matrix factorization step preserve community structure in the learned embeddings?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses matrix factorization as part of its method.
items.correction: The passage says DeepWalk learns representations by modeling a stream of short random walks, not by matrix factorization.
items.evidence_quote: We develop an algorithm ( DeepW alk) that learns social representations of a graph’s vertices, by modeling a stream of short random walks.

items.question: Under which conditions does DeepWalk outperform standard classification methods by directly predicting labels from the graph?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk directly predicts labels and is compared as outperforming standard classification methods.
items.correction: DeepWalk learns latent representations that can be exploited by standard classification methods; it does not directly predict labels in the described formulation.
items.evidence_quote: The learned representation encodes community structure so it can be easily exploited by standard classification methods.
